newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Newman Tonks spurns FKI bid.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Newman Tonks spurns FKI bid.

text.p: Acquisitive British engineering group FKI launched its first hostile takeover on Tuesday, bidding 195.7 million pounds ($325 million) in cash and shares for building supplier Newman Tonks Group.
While shares in Newman Tonks surged, the building supplier spurned the takeover bid as "opportunistic" and unsolicited. It added the bid undervalued the company,

But FKI chief executive Bob Beeston dismissed the rebuttal. "For the fifth consecutive year the management of Newman Tonks is promising jam tomorrow and asking shareholders to ignore the earnings and share price performance of the last five years," he said in a statement. FKI, with four main divisions of material handling, hardware, automotive and engineering, said Newman Tonks' businesses in Britain and Europe would complement its hardware group in North America and create an international hardware business with turnover in excess of 500 million pounds.
"The acquisition of Newman Tonks represents an excellent opportunity to expand FKI's hardware group internationally and in new sectors of the market," said chairman Jeff Whalley.

Although some traders said they expected investors to take advantage of the offer, Newman Tonks said the bid undervalued the group's brand and prospects -- especially after a restructuring over the last five years to refocus the company.
"...shareholders are urged to take no action in relation to the offer and not to sell their shares," it stated.
But FKI has already won the backing of two of its target's institutional shareholders.
M&G, Newman Tonks' largest shareholder with an 11.18 percent stake in the company, is supporting the offer along with Britannic Assurance, which has a 2.19 percent holding.

FKI's latest bid brings to an end a busy year on the acquisition front. It recently bought Italian firm Marelli Motori and the Hawker Siddeley Electric power group for a total 235 million pounds. But this is its first hostile bid.
FKI's cash and share offer for Newman Tonks, equivalent to 150 pence a share, represents a 46.3 percent premium to the firm's closing share price of 102.5p on December 13.
Newman Tonks shares hit a new year high of 151.5p on Tuesday before closing at 149.5p, a rise of 20.5p.
FKI said that over the last five years, Newman Tonks' financial and share price performance has been dismal.
Shares in Newman Tonks have traded as low as 98 pence this year. FKI said the shares have traded at a 58 percent discount relative to the FT All share index since December 16, 1991.

"1996 has been a year of misery for any holders of Newman Tonks and the stock has gone up in a straight line to the level of the bid," said one equities trader. "I would expect people are just going to say thanks very much'."
There is also a cash alternative to the offer valuing each Newman Tonks share at 140p and the company at 182.6 million pounds, representing a 36.6 percent premium to the share price.
The cash alternative will be financed partly from FKI's cash resources and from the proceeds of a conditional rights issue to raise a maximum of 152.4 million pounds.
The rights issue is on the basis of two new FKI shares for every 13 existing shares at 175 pence per share -- and is conditional upon the offer being declared unconditional.
This would take FKI's gearing to around 80 percent from the 60 percent level it had hit after buying Hawker Siddleley Electric. ($1=.6027 Pound)
